title: Add Text to an Image
about: Add Text to Image is a browser-based typography editor for placing captions, titles, labels, quotes and watermarks on a picture. Add multiple independent text layers, edit each layer until the design looks right, then export a finished image without changing the original file.
steps: Choose an image from your device, drag it into the upload area, or paste an image from your clipboard. The editor supports image formats your browser can decode and accepts files up to 25 MB.
Use Add text layer to create one or more text elements. Select a layer in the Text layers panel to edit its content and appearance.
Choose a font, size, color, alignment, bold, italic or underline styling. Use outline, shadow and a background box to improve readability.
Drag selected text directly on the image to position it. Fine-tune X and Y coordinates or use the arrow keys; hold Shift with an arrow key for larger movements.
Duplicate, hide, reorder or delete layers as needed. Choose PNG, JPG or WebP and download the final image. PNG preserves transparency; JPG flattens transparent areas onto white.
capabilities: The editor provides multiple independently editable text layers, multiline text, layer naming, selection, visibility, duplication, deletion and stacking order. Each layer supports font family, font size, text color, bold, italic, underline, left/center/right alignment, opacity, rotation, outline color and width, shadow color and blur, and a configurable background box with opacity. Text can be positioned by dragging, numeric X/Y coordinates or keyboard nudging. Export supports PNG, JPEG and WebP with quality control for lossy formats. Rendering and export use the browser Canvas API.
benefits: Create image captions, meme text, social graphics, thumbnail titles, labels and simple text watermarks without opening a full design application. The live canvas preview reflects the current layer settings, and the original source image remains unchanged.
limitations: The editor relies on image decoding, Canvas 2D and available system fonts in the browser. Font appearance can vary between devices. Animated formats such as GIF are decoded as a still image for editing; animation is not preserved. JPG cannot preserve transparency and is exported with a white background. Very large images or many complex layers can require substantial device memory. Metadata is not guaranteed to be preserved in exported files.

faqs.question: Can I add more than one text element?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use Add text layer to create multiple independently editable text elements. Select any layer to change its settings.

faqs.question: Can I move text precisely?
faqs.answer: Drag the selected text on the preview, enter its X and Y coordinates, or use the arrow keys. Hold Shift while pressing an arrow key to move it in larger steps.

faqs.question: How do I make text readable on a busy photo?
faqs.answer: Use a contrasting text color, increase the outline width, add a soft shadow, or enable a semi-transparent background box.

faqs.question: Which export formats are available?
faqs.answer: PNG, JPG and WebP. PNG is best when transparency matters; JPG is suitable for photographs; WebP can provide smaller files.

faqs.question: Are my images uploaded?
faqs.answer: The editor reads and renders the selected image locally in your browser. It does not send the image to BROBEX servers.

faqs.question: Does the editor preserve animated GIFs?
faqs.answer: No. The browser displays a decoded still frame for editing and exports a static image.
